the epistemological pursuit of truth in Bayesian artificial intelligence (AI), arguing that truth convergence is a conditional outcome rather than an inherent property of the algorithm. Bayesian reasoning guarantees formal convergence mathematically, but its alignment with reality depends on prior openness, evidence authenticity, independence, information richness, feedback mechanisms, and institutional support. The study analyzes the limitations of Bayesian convergence theorems, the learnability in open Bayesianism, AI failure modes in modern information ecologies, and design principles and ethical constraints. It emphasizes that truth convergence is not merely an algorithmic property, but a civilizational, collective, and ecological achievement. By implementing non-dogmatic priors, independent evidence channels, explicit modeling of evidence correlations, feedback loop corrections, and institutionalized epistemic humility, AI can pursue truth conditionally. Ultimately, Bayesian AI is both a tool for formal reasoning and a litmus test of civilizational epistemic capacity, providing actionable guidance for modern scientific rationality, ethical practice, \"journal-article\"}, \"abstract\": \"Abstract There is an urgent need to transition our economy, society, and culture towards systems and actions that facilitate ecological sustainability. Such radical change requires equally radical transformation of approaches to decision making and resource use. Sustainable entrepreneurship (SE) is often presented as the answer to meeting the triple‐bottom‐line challenges that businesses face; however, there are very real limits to what it can achieve. SE is in the early stages of adopting tools at the technological frontier that offer empirical guidance at every point of an entrepreneurial decision‐making process. Big Data (BD) advances the potential for artificial intelligence (AI) to inform decision making, while also charting pathways to achieve desired outcomes. So far, the interactions between AI, BD, and SE have been generally under‐studied. In this primarily conceptual paper, we address the lack of work consolidating and synthesizing these literatures. We suggest that AI and BD readily contribute to further sustainable development of the weak form, but that it also holds great promise for achieving the strong sustainability ideal. We offer two propositions regarding how the integration of AI and BD can inform/support SE. We conclude by mapping out potential avenues for future research.\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "e07334e097ec22264dc4c7799eead29902b4a6f8e3e61e03800b322ad3c95d00", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.29003/m2789.sudak.ns2022-18/170", "doi:10.1111/joes.12611", "openalex:W4300837428", "openalex:W582143926", "openalex:W7128121669", "openalex:W3156012754"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.29003/m2789.sudak.ns2022-18/170", "https://doi.org/10.1111/joes.12611", "https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1111/joes.12611"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
